outcome: Since 26 January 2024 no event establishes a reciprocity law for k-th power norm residues over arbitrary number fields. The window holds a power-residue reciprocity law over function fields (Hamahata, 2024), a rational supplementary law for one family of primes (Hirakawa et al., April 2025), Langlands-program results on Galois images and irreducibility (2025 to 2026), a proof of the geometric Langlands conjecture (2024, a geometric analogue), an OpenAI claim in quantum geometric Langlands (6 October 2026, unverified), and a Lean development reported to contain proofs of global class field theory (26 June 2026). Wikipedia’s table of Hilbert’s problems (last edited 7 October 2026) still lists the problem as unresolved, and the Simons Foundation status article (18 June 2026) rates it “It’s complicated”.
problem_asks: Unpacked from the statement alone: (a) a reciprocity law, i.e. a relation among norm-residue symbols over a field, in Hilbert’s form a product formula over the primes whose value is forced to be 1; (b) for norm residues of k-th order, i.e. k-th power norm-residue symbols; (c) for k any power of a prime (k = ℓ^m for any prime ℓ and any m ≥ 1); (d) in a general algebraic number field, i.e. an arbitrary number field K, not only ℚ, abelian extensions, or fields containing roots of unity (the statement names no such restriction); (e) the most general such law: the statement asks for the most general form and does not define ‘most general’. The statement does not mention abelian or non-abelian extensions, Artin, class field theory or Langlands; those enter only through the Wikipedia article and the literature. Parts (a) to (e) are the list each event is checked against.

events.what_happened: Emil Artin, “Beweis des allgemeinen Reziprozitätsgesetzes”, Abhandlungen aus dem Mathematischen Seminar der Universität Hamburg 5 (1927), pp. 353–363, as cited in the Wikipedia article on the problem (reference list opened; the paper itself not read). The article calls Artin’s 1924, 1927 and 1930 papers the partial solution of the problem: the reciprocity law for abelian extensions of number fields, the core of class field theory. Recorded because it is the solution of the abelian case, decades before the window.
events.delivers: A general reciprocity law for abelian extensions of number fields (Artin reciprocity). Against parts (a) to (d): it covers an arbitrary number field K but only abelian extensions. The sources read do not say it is stated for k-th power norm residues for every prime power k; the article treats it as the abelian partial answer.
events.remains: Parts (a) to (d) for non-abelian extensions, which Wikipedia links to Langlands’ 1967 letter to Weil; and part (e), the most general form.

checked_by.who: Abhandlungen aus dem Mathematischen Seminar der Universität Hamburg (journal of publication)
checked_by.qualification: a mathematics journal of the period; its refereeing practice in 1927 was not checked
checked_by.what_they_did: published the paper; later literature (Wikipedia, and the standard class field theory treatments) treats the abelian law as established

events.direction: Proves a reciprocity law in the abelian case, which Wikipedia counts as the partial solution of the problem. It points toward the problem’s kind of law, restricted to abelian extensions.

events.what_happened: Igor Shafarevich gave explicit formulas for norm residues in 1948, 1949 and 1950, per the Wikipedia article on the problem (opened). The article gives the years but not the setting. A search snippet (the source article was not opened) describes the 1950 result as an explicit formula for the Hilbert symbol at odd prime powers over general local fields. Recorded as historical partial progress.
events.delivers: Explicit formulas for norm residues (Hilbert symbols). Per the snippet, local, at odd prime powers. A local explicit formula does not state the global reciprocity law, though it supplies the local factors of the product formula in Hilbert’s form. The sources read do not settle whether that counts toward the problem.
events.remains: The global reciprocity law for k-th power norm residues over arbitrary number fields (parts (a) to (e)), and the non-abelian case.
events.doubts: Scope read from a search snippet only. The 1948 and 1949 papers were not located, so the 1948 date is the earliest year Wikipedia gives, not a checked first-argument date.
events.direction: Partial: explicit local formulas. Does not state a global law; the sources read do not say it settles any part of the problem as stated.

events.what_happened: Yoshinori Hamahata, “A reciprocity law in function fields”, Archiv der Mathematik 123 (2024), pp. 49–56, issue dated 2024/07 per the author’s institutional research record (opened). The abstract as quoted on that record: “We generalized Gauss’ lemma over function fields, and established a reciprocity law for power residue symbols. As an application, a reciprocity law for power residue symbols was established in totally imaginary function fields.” The Springer article page redirected to a login and was not read, so the first online date is not established and the date given is the year of issue only. A correction notice (10.1007/s00013-024-02092-9) appears in search results. A search summary says it concerns the open-access licence rather than the mathematics; I did not read it.
events.revisions: A correction notice exists (10.1007/s00013-024-02092-9); its content was not read.
events.delivers: A reciprocity law for power residue symbols over function fields, including totally imaginary function fields. Against the statement: the base field is a function field, not a number field, so part (d) is not met. It is an analogue, recorded because it is a reciprocity law for k-th power symbols.
events.remains: Everything for number fields: parts (a) to (e) as stated for algebraic number fields.

checked_by.who: Archiv der Mathematik (Birkhäuser, Springer) editorial process
checked_by.what_they_did: accepted and published the article (per the author’s publication record)

events.direction: Proves a reciprocity law for power residue symbols, but over function fields. The problem asks about number fields. It does not contradict the problem; it is off its scope.

events.what_happened: Yoshinosuke Hirakawa, Tomokazu Kashio, Ryutaro Sekigawa, Naoaki Takada and Shuji Yamamoto, “A note on the second supplementary law of rational power residue symbols”, arXiv:2504.11666 [math.NT]. v1 submitted 15 April 2025; v2 revised 7 June 2025, which corrected the data in Example 1.6. Full HTML text read. Theorem 1.1, as rendered: for integers m, n with p := Φ_q(n/m)·m^(q−1) prime and different from q, (q/p)_q = 1 if and only if Li_{1−q}(n/m) lies in q²ℤ_(q). It generalises Legendre’s second supplementary law to q-th power residue symbols for a prime q, through polylogarithms; the method follows Lemmermeyer’s proof of Euler’s conjectures on cubic residues. The rendered formula was garbled and this is my reading of it.
events.revisions: v1 15 Apr 2025; v2 7 Jun 2025 (corrects the data in Example 1.6).
events.delivers: Over the base field ℚ only, a criterion for (q/p)_q = 1 for primes p of one special form p = Φ_q(n/m)·m^(q−1), for prime exponent q, given as an equivalence with a polylogarithm condition. Against parts (a) to (d): base field ℚ only, one family of primes, and a supplementary law (when a symbol is trivial), not a reciprocity law among symbols over general K. It is a special case of parts (c) and (d) for K = ℚ and a narrow set of primes.
events.remains: A general reciprocity law (part (a)) over arbitrary number fields (part (d)) for all prime-power k (part (c)), and the most general form (part (e)). The criterion does not cover primes outside the special family.
events.direction: Gives an explicit criterion within the rational case. It neither confirms nor contradicts the problem.

events.what_happened: D. G. Benois, “Explicit reciprocity laws in the theory of local fields”, Chebyshevskii Sbornik 26(4) (2025), pp. 37–70, DOI 10.22405/2226-8383-2025-26-4-37-70. The article was NOT read: the journal page failed to load twice and the DOI redirect was not followed. The description comes from a search snippet. It describes a survey of explicit formulas for the Hilbert symbol and their generalisations to p-adic representations via p-adic Hodge theory, with 103 references, which the author calls incomplete and not an exhaustive guide.
events.delivers: Per the snippet only: a survey, with no new theorem claimed. Its subject is local fields (explicit reciprocity laws), not global number fields.
events.remains: Everything in parts (a) to (e) for global number fields.

checked_by.qualification: a mathematics journal; its refereeing was not checked

events.doubts: The article was not read. The scope and survey character come from a search snippet, so they should be checked against the article.
events.direction: A survey of local explicit reciprocity. It has no direction relative to the problem’s assertion.

events.what_happened: Alireza Shavali, “On the Image of Automorphic Galois Representations”, arXiv:2502.10799 [math.NT], submitted 15 February 2025 (single version). Abstract as summarised by the fetch: extra-twists for automorphic representations of GL_n are used to describe the image of the Galois representations attached to regular algebraic cuspidal automorphic representations of GL_3 over totally real fields; a conjecture for GL_n is formulated and shown to follow from standard Langlands conjectures. The author’s Heidelberg PhD thesis of the same title was defended on 23 July 2025 (search snippet). Of the HTML rendering, the first 100k of about 125k characters were read. The acknowledgements name the advisor Gebhard Böckle. The unconditional GL_3 theorem, as read: for a regular algebraic cuspidal π of general type on GL_3 over a totally real field K, with F the field fixed by all extra-twists, there is a finite extension L/K and a semisimple algebraic group H_p over F_p such that ρ_{π,p}(G_L) lies in H_p(F_p)·ℚ_p^× and is open in the p-adic topology.
events.revisions: v1 only (15 Feb 2025). A thesis version was defended July 2025 (search snippet).
events.delivers: (i) For GL_n, a conjectural description of the image of Galois representations of regular algebraic cuspidal automorphic representations, which the author says follows from standard Langlands conjectures. (ii) Unconditionally for GL_3 of general type over totally real fields, the image of the p-adic Galois representation is open in a group determined by the extra-twists. This concerns Galois representations of automorphic forms, the Langlands-correspondence side. It is not a reciprocity law for norm residues; the field is totally real; the result is for GL_3 only.
events.remains: Parts (a) to (e) of the problem. The GL_n statement is conjectural, and nothing here gives a reciprocity law among norm-residue symbols.
events.direction: Partial results on Galois images for GL_3, and a conditional conjecture for GL_n. Nothing says it contradicts the problem.

events.what_happened: Zachary Feng and Dmitri Whitmore, “Irreducibility of polarized automorphic Galois representations in infinitely many dimensions”, arXiv:2507.22631 [math.NT, math.RT]. v1 30 July 2025; v2 19 December 2025, which adds the case n = 4p and fixes minor mistakes, per the authors’ comment. The statement as read from the first 100k of about 196k characters of the HTML: for a polarized, regular algebraic, cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_n over a totally real or CM field, with 7 ∤ n and n = 4p for a prime p whenever 4 divides n, there is a set of rational primes of Dirichlet density 1 such that ρ_λ is irreducible for every λ above a prime ℓ in that set.
events.delivers: A structural statement: irreducibility of the compatible system of Galois representations for a density-one set of primes, for polarized GL_n representations under the stated restrictions. It is not a reciprocity law and does not concern norm-residue symbols.
events.remains: Parts (a) to (e) of the problem, and the reciprocity law itself.
events.direction: A structural result about Galois representations. It neither confirms nor contradicts the problem.

events.what_happened: George Boxer, Frank Calegari, Toby Gee and Vincent Pilloni, “Modularity theorems for abelian surfaces”, arXiv:2502.20645 [math.NT], submitted 28 February 2025 (single version per the abstract page). Abstract as summarised by the fetch: modularity for a positive proportion of abelian surfaces over ℚ, namely those ordinary at 3 and 3-distinguished, under assumptions on the 3-torsion representation and on the action of a decomposition group at 2. The proof uses a “2-3 switch” and a classicality theorem for ordinary p-adic Siegel modular forms. Of the HTML rendering, the first 100k of about 199k characters were read: the acknowledgements and funding were read; no AI or software mention appears in that part. A 2025 survey by Gee of the same results (arXiv:2510.02756) appears in search results and was not opened.
events.revisions: v1 only, per the abstract page.
events.delivers: Modularity, in the Langlands-correspondence sense (abelian surfaces against Siegel modular forms), for a positive proportion of abelian surfaces over ℚ under the stated ordinarity and Galois-image hypotheses. Against the problem: a case of the Langlands correspondence over ℚ, not a reciprocity law among k-th power norm residue symbols, and restricted to a proportion of abelian surfaces over ℚ.
events.remains: Parts (a) to (e) of the problem; all abelian surfaces; the general correspondence.
events.direction: Proves modularity for a subset of abelian surfaces over ℚ. The problem’s statement is not about modularity, and nothing here contradicts it.

events.what_happened: Alireza Shavali, “Irreducibility and Monodromy of Automorphic Galois Representations of GL(4)”, arXiv:2603.19768 [math.NT]. v1 submitted 20 March 2026; v2 revised 21 August 2026 (current). Only the abstract page was read. Summary: for non-self-dual regular algebraic cuspidal automorphic representations of GL(4) over totally real fields, the p-adic Galois representations are irreducible; the authors develop extra-twists in general, compute the monodromy group over ℚ in the self-dual and non-self-dual cases, and prove p-adic and residual big-image results.
events.delivers: Structural results (irreducibility, monodromy, big image) for Galois representations of GL(4) automorphic representations over totally real fields. Not a reciprocity law.
events.doubts: Abstract page only; the full text was not read.
events.direction: Structural. It neither confirms nor contradicts the problem.

events.what_happened: Dennis Gaitsgory, Sam Raskin and collaborators (D. Arinkin, D. Beraldo, L. Chen, J. Faegerman, K. Lin, N. Rozenblyum) posted a multi-part proof of the geometric Langlands conjecture. Quanta (19 July 2024, opened) says the team posted it online in February 2024, and that it runs to over 800 pages in five papers. Part I, arXiv:2405.03599 [math.AG], was first submitted 6 May 2024 (v2 11 Sep 2024; v3 30 Sep 2025). Its abstract (opened): constructs the geometric Langlands functor from the automorphic to the spectral side in the de Rham and Betti settings, and shows several versions of the conjecture equivalent. Other parts, seen only in search results and not opened: arXiv:2405.03648 (May 2024, Part II), arXiv:2409.08670 (Sept 2024, Part IV, deducing GL_n and classical groups), arXiv:2409.09856 (Sept 2024, Part V, described as concluding).
events.revisions: Quanta says posted online February 2024; this was not checked against the authors’ own site. arXiv v1 of Part I 6 May 2024; v2 11 Sep 2024; v3 30 Sep 2025.
events.delivers: Per the Part I abstract, it constructs the geometric Langlands functor in one direction and shows several versions of the conjecture equivalent. The series is described as proving the geometric Langlands conjecture. This is a geometric analogue. The number-field problem is not addressed; the link is only the shared architecture of the Langlands program.
events.remains: Parts (a) to (e) for number fields, and the Langlands conjecture for number fields.

events.what_happened: OpenAI’s openai/math repository, released with 722 manuscripts in 372 families, dated 6 October 2026 by secondary reports (the repository’s own date was not read). Family 069, “Global quantum geometric Langlands at irrational level”, has 1 manuscript. Its scope line in CONTENTS.md (read): “Proves the unramified de Rham quantum geometric Langlands equivalence for every connected simple complex algebraic group.” The README (read through a summarising fetch) describes the source as “an unreleased internal OpenAI model”. Secondary reports say OpenAI claims a “quantum” version under irrational parameters. No manuscript text for this family was read.
events.revisions: Secondary reports say three manuscripts were withdrawn a day after release (one paper had a sign error; two dependent manuscripts lost their constructions). Their identities were not read, so whether family 069 is among them is unchecked. The collection count is reported as 722 at release and 719 later.
events.delivers: Per its scope line: an equivalence in the quantum geometric Langlands setting (unramified de Rham, every connected simple complex group). This is a geometric and quantum analogue over ℂ, not a number-field statement, and it does not address norm-residue symbols.
events.remains: Parts (a) to (e) for number fields, and the Langlands conjecture over number fields.
events.doubts: A lab claim. The README says some unformalised results “could have issues”. No expert verdict on family 069 was found. General commentary on the release exists (MIT’s Andrew Sutherland, through a secondary report: “We should ask for receipts”), but it is not specific to this family.
events.direction: Claims a proof of an equivalence in a geometric and quantum setting. It is not a counterexample, and it does not address the number-field problem.

systems.name: an unreleased internal OpenAI model
systems.what_it_did: Per the repository README, the collection was produced by this model. The family 069 manuscript was not read, so it is established only that the collection came from the model, not that this family’s argument was produced by it. Secondary reports say the work came from a single prompt and a single agent, which OpenAI’s spokesperson stated and MIT’s Andrew Sutherland called unverified.

events.what_happened: Alex Best, Christopher Birkbeck, Riccardo Brasca, Eric Rodriguez Boidi, Ruben Van de Velde and Andrew Yang, “A complete formalization of Fermat’s Last Theorem for regular primes in Lean”, arXiv:2410.01466 (v1 2 Oct 2024; v2 17 Oct 2024; v3 13 Jun 2025). The paper formalises the regular case of Fermat’s Last Theorem in Lean 4, including Kummer’s lemma. Kummer’s lemma is proved via Hilbert’s Theorems 90–94 rather than class field theory (abstract and HTML). The HTML was read to its first 100k of about 111k characters. The acknowledgements thank the mathlib community and the anonymous referees of an earlier version.
events.delivers: A formal Lean proof of Fermat’s Last Theorem for regular primes, including Kummer’s lemma, by a route that avoids class field theory. Its scope is Kummer’s lemma and cyclotomic fields for regular primes. It is not a reciprocity law, and it formalises a known human proof.

checked_by.qualification: reviewers for an earlier submission; their standing is not identified
checked_by.what_they_did: reviewed an earlier version, which the authors say improved the paper’s clarity and presentation

events.direction: A formal proof of a known theorem (FLT for regular primes). It does not cut toward or against the problem’s assertion.

events.what_happened: Evan Chen, Chris Cummins, Ben Eltschig, Dejan Grubisic, Leopold Haller, Letong Hong, Andranik Kurghinyan, Kenny Lau, Hugh Leather, Seewoo Lee, Aram Markosyan, Ken Ono, Manooshree Patel, Gaurang Pendharkar, Vedant Rathi, Alex Schneidman, Volker Seeker, Shubho Sengupta, Ishan Sinha, Jimmy Xin and Jujian Zhang, “Almost all primes are partially regular”, arXiv:2602.05090 [math.NT], submitted 4 February 2026 (single version). Abstract as summarised by the fetch: for a fixed exponent α > 1/2, a prime is partially regular when certain eigenspaces of the p-part of the class group of ℚ(ζ_p) vanish for characters up to roughly √p divided by a power of log p. The authors prove that a set of primes of density one is partially regular, giving a partial Vandiver theorem for even eigenspaces on that set via Leopoldt reflection. The abstract states the density-one result was “produced automatically by AxiomProver from a natural-language statement of the conjecture” and that the proof is fully formalised in Lean/Mathlib. The first part of the text was not read.
events.delivers: A density-one result on partial regularity of the cyclotomic class groups of ℚ(ζ_p), and a partial Vandiver theorem on that set. The scope is cyclotomic class groups and Bernoulli numbers, not reciprocity laws or norm-residue symbols. Class field theory is only indirectly relevant. Discounted for this problem.
events.doubts: The authors’ own claim. The AI attribution is quoted from the abstract through a summarising fetch and should be checked against the arXiv abstract. The Lean statement’s match to the intended claim is not reported. Human reading of the paper was not found.
events.direction: Proves a density-one partial regularity statement about cyclotomic class groups. It is not about the problem.

events.what_happened: Per the Xena Project blog post of 20 July 2026 (opened): on 26 June 2026 Boris Alexeev, described there as working at OpenAI, posted on the Lean Zulip that he had steered ChatGPT to a complete formalisation of the Erdős unit-distance counterexample. The post’s words: “Boris works at OpenAI and had used their new model Sol to do the autoformalization.” The post says the development contains “a proof of some really hard theorems in global class field theory”. The unit-distance disproof is the May 2026 OpenAI result, not this problem. Alex Kontorovich’s X post, which reports a roughly 1M-line Lean formal solution that “passed eval”, appeared in search results and was not opened. The Zulip post and the repository were NOT read; the Xena post is the only source read on this event.

The post read does not say which theorems. If they include Artin’s reciprocity law, the development is a formal record of the abelian case, which is already known (see artin-1927-abelian-reciprocity). A formalisation of known theory is not a new solution. Against parts (a) to (e): abelian content only, if any, and no new law.

The post does not, as read, say which global class field theory results are formalised, or that the development is free of sorry. A search snippet said Sol generated about 1.2 million lines of Lean in three weeks; that snippet was not read at source.

events.what_happened: Minhyong Kim, “Diophantine geometry and non-abelian reciprocity laws I”, arXiv:1312.7019 [math.NT]. v1 25 December 2013; v2 5 January 2014; v3 15 May 2015, which corrected errors and replaced the fundamental group with a prime-to-2 quotient. The abstract as summarised by the fetch: uses non-abelian fundamental groups to define a sequence of higher reciprocity maps on adelic points of a variety over a number field, under Galois-cohomology conditions. The non-abelian reciprocity law says global points lie in the kernel of all these maps. Only the abstract page was read.

Against the problem: the maps are defined on varieties and are not stated as k-th power norm-residue symbols. The sources read do not say the framework reproduces the law of part (a) or the symbols of part (c).

events.doubts: Abstract page only; full text not read. Whether the framework reduces to a k-th power symbol law is not established.
events.direction: A framework for non-abelian reciprocity on varieties. It is a candidate reading of ‘non-abelian reciprocity law’, but not the problem’s symbols. It neither confirms nor contradicts the problem.

disputes.summary: The status of Problem 9 differs by source. Wikipedia’s “Hilbert’s problems” table (last edited 7 October 2026, per the fetch) reads “Unresolved”, with Artin’s abelian law as the partial result. The Simons Foundation status article (18 June 2026) rates it “It’s complicated”. A Simple English Wikipedia page and a 2017 arXiv survey on problems in mathematical physics, both seen only as search snippets and not opened, list it among partially accepted resolutions.

A 2010 Bilkent University thesis on explicit reciprocity laws (Ali Adalı; seen as a search snippet, not opened) says Vostokov and Brückner later completed the solution of Hilbert’s ninth problem through explicit reciprocity laws. Wikipedia and the Simons page do not treat the explicit local formulas as solving the problem. The Bilkent claim concerns the local explicit formulas, not the global statement.

summary: I ran 43 web searches and opened about 25 pages: the arXiv abstract and HTML pages for the 2024–2026 preprints, the Wikipedia article and table of problems, the Simons Foundation status article, the openai/math README and its full CONTENTS.md (read in chunks to the end), the Quanta article of 19 July 2024, the Xena Project blog post of 20 July 2026, and the author’s research record for Hamahata. No source reports a settlement of the problem as stated, or a bound on it, since January 2024. The status sources agree that the abelian case is Artin’s (1927) and that the non-abelian case is open, but they disagree on the label (see disputes). The window events fall into three groups. (1) Analogues and special cases, discounted by scope: Hamahata’s power-residue law over function fields; Hirakawa et al.’s supplementary law over ℚ for one family of primes; the geometric Langlands series (curves, 2024); and OpenAI family 069 (quantum geometric Langlands, 6 October 2026, unverified). (2) Langlands-program results that the Wikipedia article calls the best candidate for the general law: Boxer, Calegari, Gee and Pilloni on abelian surfaces over ℚ (2025), Shavali on GL_3 Galois images (2025) and GL(4) irreducibility (2026), and Feng and Whitmore (2025). I have recorded these as borderline. None states a law for k-th power norm residues, but the problem’s ‘most general reciprocity law’ could be read as the Langlands correspondence. (3) AI-related events. The Alexeev/Sol Lean development (26 June 2026) is reported to contain proofs of global class field theory, which is the abelian content of the problem. But it formalises an unrelated disproof, so as reported it is a formalisation of known theory. Its attribution to Sol and ChatGPT rests on Xena’s account of a Zulip post I could not open, so no system is placed in ai.systems. AxiomProver’s cyclotomic class-group paper (4 February 2026) does name an AI system in its abstract, but it is off-scope. No event on this problem names an AI system as contributing to its mathematics. Across the 372 OpenAI families, the scope lines I read show no family on this problem; family 069 is the only Langlands-related family, and it is geometric. The tenth-problem families are off-scope. Engagement: none of the 2025 preprints (Hirakawa et al., Feng and Whitmore, Boxer et al., Shavali) showed public engagement in my searches. I did not run a per-paper search for that, so no_engagement_found is null for them. Close calls: whether Langlands-program progress counts (see competing_reading); whether a Lean formalisation of global class field theory counts as AI-involved mathematics (under §5.4 it is formalisation of known theory, so probably not load-bearing); and whether Hamahata’s function-field law is an analogue that should be discounted entirely.
competing_reading: The strongest case for counting the window is that the Wikipedia article itself names Langlands’ 1967 conjecture as the best candidate for the general law. On that reading, the Langlands-program results (Boxer et al., Shavali 2025 and 2026, Feng and Whitmore) and possibly the geometric proof are progress on the problem’s named candidate, and the judging pass should weigh them. The opposite reading is that the problem asks about k-th power norm residues over arbitrary number fields. Artin’s abelian law already covers the abelian part in its own terms, and nothing in the window gives a non-abelian law for these symbols, so none of the window events moves the problem as stated. On the Alexeev/Sol item, a reader who counts a formal development of global class field theory as a new AI-assisted contribution to the abelian case would give it weight. A reader who treats formalisation of known theory as not load-bearing (§5.4) would give it none.
what_would_settle_it: (1) Whether ‘the most general reciprocity law’ in the statement means Langlands’ non-abelian correspondence, in which case the Langlands-program events are in scope, or the k-th power norm-residue law for arbitrary number fields, in which case they are not. (2) The Sol/Alexeev Lean development: which global class field theory theorems it proves (in particular whether Artin’s reciprocity law is among them), whether it is sorry-free, and the authors’ own account of the AI role, from the Zulip post or the repository. (3) The full texts of Hamahata’s first online date and correction notice, and of Benois (2025). (4) The full texts of Hirakawa et al., Feng and Whitmore, Boxer et al., and Shavali beyond the first part read, including their acknowledgements, and any published refereeing. (5) The openai/math repository’s own date, its family 045 entry (absent from the listing), the withdrawn-manuscript list, and the manuscript text of family 069.

events.credibility_reason: Unread lab claim with no expert engagement; the release had withdrawals and the README warns unformalised results could have issues.

events.ai_basis: produced automatically by AxiomProver from a natural-language statement of the conjecture

judgement.why: The statement asks for the most general reciprocity law for prime-power norm residues over arbitrary number fields. Only Artin's 1927 abelian law settles a restriction of it (case, digested by long acceptance, pre-snapshot). No window event gives a reciprocity law for norm residues over number fields. Function-field, geometric and quantum-geometric Langlands work changes the base setting, and the GL_n Galois-image and modularity results concern a different question, so all are variant. Hirakawa et al. is a supplementary criterion over Q for one prime family, where the general law over Q is already known, so it is variant, not case. The Lean items formalise known or unrelated theory, so they are none. The AI events (OpenAI 069, AxiomProver) are credited as generated in their own rows, but both are off-scope. The close call is whether Langlands-program results count as progress on 'the most general law'. I read the statement's own words, about norm-residue symbols, as excluding them.
judgement.doubts: Hamahata's date is year-only 2024, so it cannot be placed. Shafarevich's local formulas could arguably be a pre-snapshot case. That does not change the outcome, because no pre-snapshot event is whole.
